claims.claim_text: The indexed John P. Browne is confirmed as the Army entrant represented by the exact full-name and private-identifier match in the official merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The full name and private service identifier match across the OSS index and official Army-entry file; the identifier is withheld.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by an exact private identifier and exact full indexed name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army-entry record is dated October 26, 1942; the index documents an OSS personnel file but not the OSS transfer date.
claims.match_notes: The Army record supports enlisted Army status. Its civilian occupation is modeled separately and does not establish an employer or Army-to-OSS sequence.

claims.claim_text: The indexed William B. Browne is a high-confidence match to Capt. William B. Browne, documented by an official CIA history in OSS/X-2 at Steyerling, Austria, in May 1945.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Capt. William B. Browne in Steyerling, Austria
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official history names Capt. William B. Browne in an X-2 operation based in Steyerling near the end of the war.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact full indexed name, exact middle initial, compatible officer status, and explicit OSS/X-2 context. The public history omits the private identifier and Box 87 has not been reviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history places Browne in X-2 in May 1945; it supplies no OSS entry date or pre-OSS occupation.
claims.match_notes: The official Army merged file returned no exact private-identifier row, which is compatible with its officer exclusion and is not treated as disproof. No pre-OSS employer is inferred.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Evelyn C. Brownell is a high-confidence match to the exact-name subject whose Washington Post obituary explicitly records work for the Office of Strategic Services.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A reputable obituary for Evelyn C. Brownell explicitly includes OSS among her early-career workplaces.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact full name and direct OSS statement in a reputable obituary. The index supplies no private identifier and Box 87 has not been reviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: The obituary places OSS early in her career but does not give dates or explicitly establish whether the Forest Service or private-lawyer work immediately preceded or followed OSS.
claims.match_notes: The U.S. Forest Service and lawyer James J. Laughlin are not modeled as pre-OSS affiliations because the obituary does not explicitly date or sequence them. No employer is silently inferred.
